text:
Sam: quick RFC follow-up — thinking about moving RBAC evaluation for console dashboards into the projection / materialized view layer rather than doing auth joins at query time. reduces per-request fanout and should cut p95 on expensive panels by a lot. any obvious red flags?

Claire: interesting. my main worry is role churn. if we materialize role-views per-tenant/user, updates could be expensive or eventually inconsistent. what's the invalidation window?

Sam: good call. proposal is: maintain a small role-version counter on the tenant row and include it in materialized keys. on role change we enqueue invalidation to the projection worker. target window: < 30s for typical changes. longer for backfilled migrations.

Raj: two perf concerns: 1) write amplification on user/role churn (we have tenants with thousands of users) 2) storage growth for per-role projections. both could be problematic. do we have anything like prefix compaction to keep storage bounded?

Sam: agree. my thinking: we don't create per-user projections for everyone — we create per-authorization-segment projections. common patterns: org-admin vs read-only vs custom role groups. for high-cardinality cases we fall back to runtime filter join. so it's hybrid.

Tessa: hybrid sounds sensible. can we quantify break-even? e.g., at what cardinality do we lose benefit and fall back? need numbers for the RFC follow-up.

Sam: yes — next steps: run two benchmarks on staging dataset: (A) projection-pushdown with materialized auth segments + invalidation, (B) existing join-on-read. measure p50/p95, CPU, write QPS, and storage. also simulate role-change bursts.

Claire: also add a test for eventual-consistency UX: deploy a role flip and ensure console shows stale state for < 30s with explicit banner. product wants graceful behavior.

Raj: operational-wise we need an engineer-facing knob to disable materialization per-tenant. some large customers will prefer the join approach. add that to the rollout plan.

Sam: rollout plan draft: 1) implement projection + invalidation spike on staging (2w) 2) perf bench and storage model (3w) 3) feature-flagged canary on 5% of traffic with per-tenant opt-out (2w) 4) measure error/latency regressions, product sign-off, then ramp.

Tessa: what about migrations? if we switch for a tenant we need to build their projection. do we do live build or background backfill?

Sam: background backfill via projection workers; we avoid blocking reads by serving join-on-read until projection ready. we should provide a migration endpoint that triggers backfill for a tenant and returns status.

Raj: please add SLO acceptance criteria in the RFC follow-up: max added tail latency, max storage per tenant, and tolerable staleness. also include rollback criteria for canary.

Sam: will draft update with numbers. quick note: deploy-bot: triggered canary job for authz-projection spike on staging earlier, logs are here: https://ci.internal/redwood/authz-proj/17685

deploy-bot: build 17685 succeeded — projection worker spike deployed to staging (sam/raj/tessa set as approvers).

Claire: nice. thanks. i'll paste UI banner copy in the RFC doc for the stale-state message.

Sam: thanks all. i'll put the bench plan + metrics table into the RFC follow-up and ping for approvals.
